doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

chapter: Discovering jazz in Sweden and at Hamilton
title: Eddie Durham and Roger Ramirez of the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band
summary: Vollmer notes Durham arranged the Joe Loss cover and later played in his band for 11 years; he calls Durham and Ramirez exceptional musical geniuses.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: recording was an arrangement by Eddie Durham. And Eddie Durham later on was in the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band for 11 years. And he also plays on Glenn Miller’s “Slip Horn Jive” which I think he wrote that. And Eddie Durham, as far as I’m concerned, there were two exceptional — I’ll call them American musical geniuses, two exceptional musicians who have gone through the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band. One was Roger Ram Ramirez, the pianist, and the other was Eddie Durham. And Eddie Durham, it was a whole education to be around him. Because he was very modest but he had done an awful lot.
